answer.evidence: The object is a square door frame facing south with a dark stairwell inside. The lintel (rows 1-5) is a front-facing strip: row 1 is a light outline line, then rows 2-5 are mid and dark bands with no eave shadow, so it is not a top surface. The stair treads are only 1-row light lines (rows 18 and 23) sitting directly above the vertical step faces (rows 19-21 and 24-28). No tread is deeper than 1-2 rows, and no roof slope, ellipse or visible contents show a horizontal surface. The side jambs are flat vertical strips. Only a rim-level top of about 2 rows is present, so the drawing reads as a flat front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small stair-down alcove in a grey stone frame with dark steps inside. It shows 6 visible tones per tile against 7 for castle-wall-n-window2 and 15 for castle-door2-closed, so it is close to the wall reference and well under the door. Near-flat coverage is 8%, in line with the references at 1% and 9%. Its dark edge pixels are 100% neutral, but the references are also 100% neutral, so the outline matches shipped wizarding_world art and is not a deficiency against this standard. The frame has a highlight, mid and dark ramp with some stone texture, and the stair interior has stepped bands. It reads as a bit simpler and flatter than the references, with a thinner frame and fewer per-stone details. Not much lower, but a careful artist might see it as slightly thin next to them.
